writeup.headline: Intel rates Sell: strong balance sheet and growth outweighed by steep valuation, weak margins and a disappointing outlook.
writeup.thesis: Intel scores 42, a Sell, held down mainly by valuation (score 7): in absolute terms the multiples are high at 8.2x sales, 129.9x free cash flow and 275.5x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 4.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and P/S is more expensive than at 56 of the last 61 month-ends. Quality is weak (score 39), with a 2.9% operating margin, a 6.3% FCF margin and diluted share count up 17.1% year on year. News risk (score 32) reflects Q4 guidance of $15–16B revenue and $0.25 non-GAAP EPS, well below consensus, followed by several downgrades. Offsetting this, growth is decent (score 59) with TTM revenue growth of 12.1%, though growth slowed by 4.5 pp from the previous quarter, and the balance sheet is strong (score 93) with net cash. The trend score of 47 is middling, with the price 34.7% below its 52-week high and shares 10.1 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Q4 guidance well below consensus and management expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of next year
High absolute valuation leaves little room for further disappointment
Thin 2.9% operating margin and heavy dilution, with diluted share count up 17.1% year on year
Analyst downgrades from BofA, Roth and Seaport Global, with concerns that data-center products are not yet technically competitive
Price 9.4% below its 50-day average and lagging SPY and QQQ
what_would_change: A 3-point score gain would lift the rating to Hold, for example from improved news sentiment if foundry customer wins are confirmed
Better operating margins or slower share dilution would raise the quality score
A fall of 13 points would push it to Strong Sell, for example if growth decelerates sharply or guidance is cut further
A lower share price relative to sales and cash flow would lift the very low valuation score
